items.q: What went wrong when a web-connected agent answered an investing question?
items.a: It used **one or two of 15 sources**, relied on a **three-month-old note**, and admitted it couldn't find consensus.

items.q: What changed when the same agent was connected to the Vault?
items.a: It scoped to **the right week**, found **52 candidates** and cited **seven**.

items.q: Which enrichment matters most on each Vault document?
items.a: The **time period discussed**, alongside countries, concepts and markets.

items.q: What do human readers need from search?
items.a: **Precision**: people read about **300 words a minute**.

items.q: What do agent readers need from search?
items.a: **Scale**: they read ~100x faster and fire **100+ queries per second**.

items.q: How did Bridgewater respond to 'Vault search is bad'?
items.a: Hand-built a **~200-question benchmark** in under a week: **precision@10 was ~60%**, later 90-95%.

items.q: Why is post-filtering risky for filtered RAG queries?
items.a: The globally nearest results may not match the filter, so **recall drops**.
Searches only **nearest clusters with matches**: near pre-filter recall at **post-filter speed**.

items.q: How did Bridgewater get researchers to actually use the Vault?
items.a: Rebuilt their email habits: subscription lists became **saved searches**, folders became **saved collections**.

items.q: Which interface did they build for agents?
How does the Vault compound knowledge?
items.a: It writes each **human-agent synthesis back into the corpus** for the next question.
